requirements.requirement: Run an operational Vault Transit seal provider on node1.
requirements.summary: node1's Vault service is active and enabled, unsealed with file storage, and exposes the requested AES256-GCM96 Transit key.

requirements.requirement: Use CA-validated TLS and allow every Raft member to use the Transit service.
requirements.summary: Certificates for all four nodes validate against the private CA with appropriate SANs. node2, node3, and node4 each completed a TLS-verified Transit encrypt/decrypt round trip using renewable, limited-policy credentials.

requirements.requirement: Build a three-member Vault cluster on node2, node3, and node4 using integrated Raft storage, with all members as healthy voters.
requirements.summary: The cluster initialized with Raft storage and HA enabled. Final Autopilot state shows all three nodes alive, healthy, synchronized at the same term/index, and in the voter set with failure tolerance one.

requirements.requirement: Automatically unseal Raft members with Transit after restart.
requirements.summary: A bounded restart of initialized node2 showed the healthy baseline, complete service stop, restart as seal type transit with sealed=false, stored-key unseal log entries, and subsequent healthy voter recovery. Final checks show all three members currently use the Transit seal and are unsealed.

requirements.requirement: Enable versioned KV at secret/ and store proof=raft-auto-unseal at secret/infraset.
requirements.summary: secret/ reports KV version 2, and the requested proof value persisted through the outage and is readable from every Raft member.

requirements.requirement: Place usable administrative access variables in /root/vault-admin.env on every Raft member.
requirements.summary: Each member has a root-owned mode-600 environment file containing address, CA, client certificate/key, and token variables; each file was sourced successfully to authenticate and read the proof secret.

requirements.requirement: Keep Vault available with one Raft member down and return the recovered member to the voter set.
requirements.summary: The three-voter baseline was captured, leader node2 was stopped with listeners absent, node3 became leader and successfully wrote/read KV data, and node2 was restored. Final state shows all three healthy voters and synchronized data.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Evidence directly covers the configured state and the full single-member failure transition: healthy baseline, leader outage, successful service through the surviving quorum, Transit-based automatic unseal on restoration, and recovery to three synchronized voters.
limitations: Only node2 received an explicit post-initialization restart test; node3 and node4 have matching configuration and final Transit/unsealed status but were not independently restart-tested.
The disruption restarted the Vault service rather than rebooting the operating system.
Lifecycle snapshots are bounded and do not inventory every filesystem path or permission.

operational_hygiene.summary: Final snapshots show no failed services or package-manager damage on any node; the new Vault listeners and systemd private directories are task-required runtime state. A deduction applies because the private CA signing key was made readable by the vault service group, and installer log/PID artifacts were created under /var/tmp without captured cleanup.
